subject: SilverLake AZ1 service bleed — temporary cross-region swap request
messages:
From: ops@silverlake-analytics.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: jane.kim@silverlake-analytics.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: URGENT: AZ1 high latency + 5xx spike (SilverLake production)

Mina / Redwood team,

We're seeing a rapid degradation across our SilverLake production endpoints in us-east-az1 starting ~08:55 UTC. Symptoms: median latency jumping from 200ms to 18-22s for many requests and a 5xx rate ~10% for the last 15 minutes. Our customers are seeing failed inference jobs.

Attached is a short screenshot of SLO graphs and the request IDs. Can Redwood either route us to another region (us-west-2) immediately or put an emergency mitigation in place? Latency is blocking key flows for our product.

Attachments (referenced): silverlake_latency_jun14.png (image/png)

Please advise asap — we need something within the hour.

--
Jane Kim
Head of Platform Ops, SilverLake Analytics
ops@silverlake-analytics.com
From: mina_haddad@redwood.com
To: ops@silverlake-analytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:28:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: AZ1 high latency + 5xx spike (SilverLake production)

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads up and the screenshots. We're on it.

Immediate options we can execute now (need your OK):
- Canary cross-region routing: route 20-25% of traffic to us-west-2 (pre-warm endpoints) for 15–30m, monitor error/latency; if healthy, ramp to 100%.
- Model degradation: pin to a lower-compute model variant for 30–60m (reduces token cost but may change quality).
- Rate-limited ingress: apply a short throttling policy for non-critical endpoints to reduce tail amplification.

If you want the fastest customer-visible fix, the canary region-swap is our recommendation. We'll need explicit approval to change routing for production traffic and to notify your compliance/ops if there are any data-residency constraints.

Marissa (SRE) — can you confirm capacity and warm-up time in us-west-2?
Rishi/Ben — looping in for visibility in case exec escalation or credits are needed.

--
Mina Haddad
Technical Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, ops@silverlake-analytics.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: AZ1 high latency + 5xx spike (SilverLake production)

On 2028-06-14 09:28 UTC Mina wrote:
> If you want the fastest customer-visible fix, the canary region-swap is our recommendation.

We have capacity in us-west-2. Pre-warm estimate: 7–12 minutes for the model profile SilverLake is on (large-quantized). Caveats: cold KV cache will cause a temporary token/latency hit for the first few requests, and we may see a short period of higher token consumption while caches populate.

Suggested plan (technical):
1) Start canary at 10:15 UTC -> route 25% traffic to us-west-2.
2) Monitor 5xx and P99 latency over 10m windows. Success criteria: 5xx < 1% and P99 <= 1s over baseline-adjusted target.
3) If canary healthy at 10:40 UTC, ramp to 100% in controlled steps (50% -> 75% -> 100%) with 5–10 minute watch windows.
4) Keep AZ1 serving until full ramp completes as fallback.

Risks: ongoing background issue in AZ1 may persist and cause oscillation if we just route; recommend we keep an active remediation ticket and root cause work parallel to swap.

I will coordinate the routing change and post metrics to the incident.

--
Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — we approve the canary at 25% and the ramp sequence. Two constraints:
- No cross-border data movement. Both regions are within the US so that should be OK.
- Please avoid model-change options for now; we prefer routing vs changing inference behavior.

Please confirm start time and any customer-facing maintenance note we should send.

Subject: Incident summary & next steps — SilverLake AZ1 routing swap completed

Team / SilverLake,

Summary of actions taken today (timeline):
- 10:15 UTC: initiated 25% canary to us-west-2.
- 10:28 UTC: canary metrics stable (5xx ~0.4%, P99 back to ~320ms).
- 11:05 UTC: ramp to 100% completed (gradual steps, final cutover 11:05 UTC).
- 11:12 UTC: observed steady state — latency restored to baseline, 5xx < 0.5%.

Impact: User-visible traffic for SilverLake production was routed away from us-east-az1 to us-west-2; SilverLake reported service restoration and no further customer-facing errors logged. We kept AZ1 as a fallback while the SRE team investigates the root cause.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: full RCA ticket (RWINF-4251) capturing root cause analysis, mitigation, and remediation timeline. Target: draft within 48 hours.
- Mina/Rishi: customer comms and credit estimate for any SLO breach.
- Infra: run post-swap health tests and burn-in in us-west-2; monitor for cache-related regressions.

Attachments: post_swap_metrics.csv (summary of latency/5xx by region and timestamps).

We'll follow up with a 30-min post-incident call today at 18:00 UTC to walk through the RCA draft and credits. Mina — please coordinate meeting invite and distribution list.

Thanks to Jane and the SilverLake team for rapid approval and to Marissa's on-call team for the fast execution.

--
Ben Carter
